text:
alex: Heads-up — we've been seeing sustained queue growth in eu-west 1 for the past 30m. Streaming threads show higher tail latency and a rising dropped-requests counter when non-streaming batch jobs spike.

priya: Saw that. graph looks like a sawtooth: streaming latency jumps, then bulk ramps, then streaming gets clipped. do we have recent admission logs?

jamal: log snippet from the admission controller (last 10m):
```
2026-03-17T18:02:11Z INFO admit request id=0x7f2 stream=yes tokens=24 route=eu-west pool=gpu-rt-1 admit=false reason=capacity_backpressure
2026-03-17T18:02:12Z INFO admit request id=0x80 batch=no stream=no tokens=512 route=eu-west pool=gpu-rt-1 admit=true
2026-03-17T18:02:13Z WARN admission_smoothing window=60s stream_headroom=0.12 bulk_headroom=0.02
```

nina: That's the admission_smoothing log we added. The smoothing window is currently 60s and favors batch throughput. When both traffic shapes ramp, streaming loses the headroom every 40-50s.

cheng: We need a quick mitigation while we design a long-term config: propose a "soft-degradation" grace period for streaming RPCs — allow 200ms additional enqueue time before preempting, instead of immediate drop or eviction. This should reduce client-visible errors.

alex: +1 for graceful enqueue. How will that interact with token buckets and prefix caching? we can't let graces accumulate and blow memory.

jamal: Implementation idea: mark streaming requests as "graceable" and attach a grace_deadline = now + 200ms. Admission loop checks: if pool is low but total_grace_memory < threshold, temporarily accept into short-lived buffer. If threshold exceeded, fall back to current preempt policy.

priya: Could we instead do dynamic grace based on observed packet RTT? e.g., grace = min(500ms, 4 * avg_roundtrip_stream) — so grace scales per-region. eu-west has ~40ms RT so that'd be 160ms, which matches Cheng's suggestion roughly.

cheng: Yes, dynamic grace seems safer. Also add a per-customer concurrent_grace cap to prevent noisy tenants from hogging ephemeral capacity.

ops-bot: Alert: eu-west GPU utilization 2m average = 94%. Streaming queue length = 87. Bulk job ramp detected at 18:02:10Z.

nina: One more constraint: our KV cache memory is pinned per-stream slot. If we accept more graceable streams, KV working set grows. We should account for estimated additional KV size in the "grace memory" budget.

alex: Agreed. Can we do a quick config change to reduce batch admission priority for the next 10 minutes to test impact? i.e., reduce batch_max_inflight by 20% and enable 200ms static grace for streams only in eu-west.

jamal: I can push a canary to eu-west: change admission config in configmap "admission-eu" -> set batch_priority_scale: 0.8 and stream_grace_ms: 200. Rolling to 3/6 pools, will monitor.

priya: Please add a tracing tag so we can filter grace hits: trace.tag=grace_euw_expt. Also dump admission metrics: grace_accepted, grace_rejected, grace_kv_bytes.

jamal: canary pushed to pools a/b/c at 18:03:40Z. Logs now showing grace=200 for streaming.

sre-bot: Deploy event: admission-config update by jamal at 2026-03-17T18:03:40Z -> rollout started to pools [eu-west-a, eu-west-b, eu-west-c].

alex: Early telemetry? any reduction in dropped streaming requests?

jamal: After 2m: grace_accepted=312, grace_rejected=78, stream_drops decreased 34% vs baseline, tail latency p999 down 28ms. Bulk throughput minor dip ~3%.

nina: KV budget impact: estimated additional KV = ~220MB across the canary pools — within our temporary headroom. Good sign.

cheng: Next steps for long-term: design adaptive admission scoring that uses exponential smoothing on both stream and bulk arrival rates, plus an urgency score from client metadata (interactive=true). Then compute a per-pool soft_headroom that reserves X% for streaming during ramps.

priya: That matches my notes from the last infra strategy sync. Also we should surface a "grace SLA" in console so product teams know some streams may be temporarily queued instead of being dropped.

alex: Action items:
- jamal: rollback if errors spike, otherwise expand canary to remaining pools in 20m. (done)
- nina: run a tabletop for KV growth scenarios and set a hard cap for grace memory.
- cheng/priya: draft admission scoring RFC with formulas and example configs.

jamal: Expanding canary to all eu-west pools at 18:12:03Z. Monitoring live.

ops-bot: eu-west canary expansion complete at 2026-03-17T18:12:03Z.

priya: Thanks team. If we see customer regressions open a postmortem ticket and tag support.

alex: Nice quick win. We'll reconvene for the RFC. :thumbsup:
